solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: First-class fruity dessert turned cold

parts.note: A is the top grade, as in A1

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the pudding is read backwards

parts.note: a fool is a pudding of puréed fruit folded into cream

explanation.surface: A top-quality fruit pudding has been sent back because it arrived cold.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British dessert of stewed fruit and cream or custard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof is distant and unfriendly, which is a figurative sense of cold.

clue.text: Skilled American department

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
dept is the standard abbreviation for department

explanation.surface: An American government department staffed by capable people.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept means highly proficient, so it is a synonym of skilled.

clue.text: One of eight cult poet edited

indicators.note: an edited text has been reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: One of eight poems by a cult poet has been edited.
explanation.definitionFit: An octuplet is any of eight babies born in a single birth, hence one of eight.

clue.text: Female managed company in general

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
to run a business is to manage it
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A woman ran a company in a general way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as a phrase meaning broadly, but 'general' is the definition and 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Franco was the Spanish general who ruled Spain as dictator from 1939 to 1975.

clue.text: Frilly trousers for one gift

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the first word holds the next one inside it

parts.note: lacy trimming is frilly
e.g. means for example, for one

explanation.surface: Someone receives a pair of frilly trousers as a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like a garment, but it is the verb: to trouser is to pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is something left to a person in a will, a gift bequeathed after death.

clue.text: Surprise — dangerous action cut short

indicators.note: cut short means its tail is clipped off, losing the last letter

parts.note: a stunt is a daring, risky feat

explanation.surface: Shock as a risky stunt is abruptly halted.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish someone, a stronger synonym of surprise used as a verb.

clue.text: Notice doctor edging away from messy place someone lives

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: taking away the edges leaves only the middle of the word

parts.note: messy without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A doctor notices someone sidling out of an untidy home.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is the location of the house or flat where a person resides.

clue.text: Went back and applied alternative medicine?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: gave a patient a different treatment

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split into RE- plus TREATED, treating again with something else.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to withdraw from a position; re-treated means given a fresh course of treatment.

clue.text: Pop star was flirty to cooks

indicators.note: to cook something is to mix and transform its ingredients, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A pop star flirted with the kitchen staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Taylor Swift is an American singer-songwriter, one of the best-selling pop stars ever.

clue.text: Run from former lover, party barely over

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the kept letters are read the other way
barely suggests stripped bare, so the word loses its outer covering and keeps only its middle

parts.note: the word party with its first and last letters stripped

explanation.surface: Someone flees an ex-partner once a party is barely finished.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a run scored without the bat, such as a wide or a bye, is an extra; 'Run' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket scoring, an extra is a run credited to the batting side that no batter hit.

clue.text: Longer period of time with new English queen

parts.note: a year is a period of time
N is the abbreviation for new
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A longer stretch of time arrives with a new English queen on the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Longer' looks like the comparative of long, but it is one who longs.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearner is a person who yearns, so one who longs for something.

clue.text: Very hot, avoiding river current

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep it out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: tropical weather is very hot
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: In sweltering heat, swimmers keep away from a river's current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like a flow of water to go with the river, but here it is the adjective meaning up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: A topical subject is one of present interest, so topical is a synonym of current in that sense.

clue.text: Mountain of work overwhelming extremely lazy maiden

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the work surrounds what follows

parts.note: opus is Latin for a work, especially a musical one

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of lazy
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A mountain of work buries an idle young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, written M.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympus is the Greek peak where the gods were said to live, so a named example of a mountain.

clue.text: Metal implant reconfigured to protect you

indicators.note: protecting something means wrapping round it, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
to reconfigure is to rearrange the parts, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A metal implant has been redesigned to keep you safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious silvery-white metallic element, used in jewellery and in medical implants.

clue.text: Practices fighting politicians to save university

parts.note: war is fighting

indicators.note: to save something is to hold on to it, so these letters are kept inside

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Politicians squabble over rescuing a university's finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practices' looks like a verb or a GP's surgery, but it is the plural noun for practice sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm-ups are short preparatory exercise sessions, so they are practices before the main event.

clue.text: Head of curly hair on first-class performer

parts.note: A is the top grade, as in A1

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, at the front

parts.note: the opening letter of curly
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A star performer is admired for a head of curly hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down clue puts the earlier pieces after the first-class letter: the head and hair sit on A.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a woman who performs in plays or films, so a kind of performer.

clue.text: Avoid European school we set up

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
sch is the abbreviation for school

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised, so the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A European school we established tries to keep clear of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew is to deliberately abstain from or shun, so it is a formal synonym of avoid.

clue.text: Use some Lurpak or Anchor for deep-fried vegetables

definitions.note: plural, but pakora is used as a collective noun for a dish of them

indicators.note: using only some of the words means taking a run of consecutive letters from inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the brand names

explanation.surface: Fry your vegetables in a brand of butter such as Lurpak or Anchor.
explanation.walkthrough: Lurpak and Anchor are brands of butter sold in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pakora is an Indian snack of vegetables dipped in spiced gram-flour batter and deep-fried.

clue.text: Rich wife functioning well without husband

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a body that works well is healthy
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A well-off wife is doing perfectly fine without her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy and rich are synonyms, both meaning having plenty of money.

clue.text: Bear moving idly, conserving energy

indicators.note: to conserve is to keep safe, so the rearranged letters hold the next one
something moving is shifting about, so the letters change places

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A bear ambles lazily about, saving its energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb: a tree bears fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to produce, as a crop or investment does, which is a sense of bear.

clue.text: Mother left a letter in Greek book

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
chi is the 22nd letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A mother has left a letter tucked inside a Greek book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek book' looks like the definition, but Greek belongs to the letter and the book is just 'book'.
explanation.definitionFit: Malachi is the last book of the Old Testament, so an example of a book of the Bible.

clue.text: Ugly look from Shakespearean character to the audience

indicators.note: what reaches an audience is what they hear, so the sound counts and not the spelling

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean actor gives the audience an unpleasant glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, lascivious or malicious look, which makes it an unpleasant glance.

clue.text: Unit in uniform invading previously

indicators.note: an invader goes inside a territory, so this letter is placed within the next word

parts.note: once means at some earlier time
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A military unit in uniform once mounted an invasion.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: Stern peer bothered host

indicators.note: bothered means disturbed or ruffled, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A severe aristocrat was put out by the person hosting him.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter fronts a television or radio programme, which is what a host does.

clue.text: Directed the setter to plug charity

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so this goes into the middle of the next word

parts.note: aid is help given to those in need
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker was told to promote a charitable cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim something is to point or direct it at a target, so aimed matches directed.
